# WebMCP

*Standard*

A proposed web standard that lets a page expose its actions as tools that AI agents in the browser can call.

**Glossary** (*WebMCP*): Web Model Context Protocol: a proposed web standard that lets a site declare the actions it offers AI agents, through declarative HTML annotations or imperative tools. Chrome offers it for testing through an origin trial or a flag.

Narrative: the topic [AI crawlers and agents on your site](../topics/ai-crawlers-and-agents.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

6 claims mention it: 1 from Google's documentation, 5 shown or said at the event (1 not in Google docs, 3 confirmed by Google docs, 1 nothing to verify). A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [WebMCP](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp).

- [`D1-C316`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Docs: Chrome's WebMCP documentation describes WebMCP as a proposed web standard that site owners can test through an origin trial starting in Chrome 149 or through a Chrome flag for local development. `[D1-C316, docs, Chrome for Developers, https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C303`](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Combining schema-based interfaces with web standards such as WebMCP lets a site expose tools to AI agents, which can then operate the interfaces, for example to test them. `[D2-C303, stage, Erin Sparling, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C281`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: A community speaker presented WebMCP (Web Model Context Protocol) as a way for a site to declare the actions it offers to AI agents, for example booking an appointment in a calendar, so an agent does not have to scrape the interface; the speaker called it faster, easier and cheaper. `[D1-C281, stage, Carlos Ortega, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C282`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: A community speaker said that at the time of the event (30 September 2026) WebMCP was not supported by all browsers but could be enabled for testing through browser flags. `[D1-C282, stage, Carlos Ortega, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C283`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: A community speaker said WebMCP has two kinds of tools: declarative ones, mostly HTML annotations such as the fields of a contact form, and imperative ones for other actions such as booking, filtering a catalogue, adding products to a cart, getting product specs or reordering. `[D1-C283, stage, Carlos Ortega, Day 1]`
- [`D1-C284`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, nothing to verify: A community speaker summed up agent readiness in three layers: a good CLS improves how agents see content, schema, landmarks and ARIA how they understand it, and WebMCP how they interact with it. `[D1-C284, stage, Carlos Ortega, Day 1]`
